quests.instruction: A ship, a ferry, and a canoe all travel on which of these?
quests.hint: All three need something that lets them float.
quests.explanation: Boats and ships travel on water, such as seas, rivers, and lakes. Their shapes are built to float and move through it.
quests.funFact: About 70 percent of Earth's surface is covered by water.

quests.instruction: Airplanes, helicopters, and small planes all travel through which of these?
quests.hint: Look up. That is where they go.
quests.explanation: Aircraft travel through the air, high above the ground. They use wings or spinning blades to stay up there.
quests.funFact: Most passenger jets cruise about ten kilometres above the ground.

quests.instruction: Cars, buses, and trucks mostly travel on which of these?
quests.hint: They all have rubber tyres that grip a hard, flat surface.
quests.explanation: Cars, buses, and trucks drive on roads. Roads give wheeled vehicles a smooth, firm surface to travel along.
quests.funFact: Some of the oldest paved roads in the world are thousands of years old.

quests.instruction: Which kind of ground makes skis and sleds a better way to travel than wheels?
quests.hint: Wheels would sink into this cold, soft white ground.
quests.explanation: Skis and sleds glide over snow because they spread out weight and slide easily. Wheels would get stuck.
quests.funFact: Some snowy towns use special winter tyres with deep grooves for extra grip.

quests.instruction: Which hot, sandy place has very few roads, so vehicles need strong tyres and plenty of water?
quests.hint: Think of dunes, heat, and very little rain.
quests.explanation: Deserts are dry and sandy, and roads can be far apart. Travellers plan carefully and carry extra water and fuel.
quests.funFact: Drivers in deserts sometimes let a little air out of their tyres to grip sand better.

quests.instruction: Roads here twist back and forth in sharp bends to climb a steep slope. Where are you?
quests.hint: The road goes up and up, and the views get wider.
quests.explanation: Mountain roads zigzag so that vehicles can climb gently instead of going straight up a steep hill.
quests.funFact: Some mountain roads are closed in winter because of heavy snow.

quests.instruction: Where would you see buses, trams, taxis, and traffic lights all packed close together?
quests.hint: Look for tall buildings and crowds of people going to work.
quests.explanation: Cities have lots of people in a small space, so they need many kinds of transport and signals to keep everyone moving.
quests.funFact: In many city centres, buses and trams have lanes of their own.

quests.instruction: Which place is surrounded by water, so you usually have to arrive by boat or plane?
quests.hint: Water lies on every side of it.
quests.explanation: An island is land with water all around it. People reach islands by ferry, boat, or plane, and sometimes by a long bridge.
quests.funFact: Some islands are joined to the mainland by long bridges, but many can only be reached by ferry or plane.

quests.instruction: Which place has fields and barns, where trucks collect crops to take to markets?
quests.hint: Look for open land where food is grown.
quests.explanation: Farmland is where crops grow. Tractors work in the fields, and trucks carry the harvest to shops and markets.
quests.funFact: Very wide farm machines sometimes need extra care when they use public roads.

quests.instruction: There is no bridge over a narrow, calm river. Which could carry two people to the other side?
quests.hint: Choose the one that floats.
quests.explanation: A small boat like a canoe can carry a few people across calm water. A bus or tractor would sink.
quests.funFact: For thousands of years, rivers were among the main routes for travel and trade.

quests.instruction: Heavy snow has blocked every road to a mountain village, and someone needs urgent medical help. Which can reach them?
quests.hint: It does not need a road and can land in a small space.
quests.explanation: A helicopter can fly over blocked roads and land in small spaces, so it can reach places vehicles on wheels cannot.
quests.funFact: Mountain rescue teams use helicopters with winches to lift people to safety.

quests.instruction: A family wants to reach a country across the ocean by tomorrow. Which is the only choice quick enough?
quests.hint: Only one of these can cross the ocean in a few hours.
quests.explanation: Airplanes fly much faster than ships and can cross oceans in hours. Trains cannot cross the sea at all.
quests.funFact: Crossing the Atlantic by ship takes about a week, but by plane it takes around seven or eight hours.

quests.instruction: Which weather makes it hard to see the road, so drivers switch on their headlights and slow down?
quests.hint: The air looks like a thick, grey cloud close to the ground.
quests.explanation: Fog hides the road ahead. Slowing down and using lights helps drivers see, and be seen, in time to stop.
quests.funFact: Some airports have special landing systems that help planes land safely in fog.

quests.instruction: Which weather makes roads wet and slippery, so cars need more space to stop?
quests.hint: Think of puddles, umbrellas, and windscreen wipers.
quests.explanation: Wet roads give tyres less grip, so vehicles take longer to stop. Drivers slow down and leave a bigger gap.
quests.funFact: On a wet road, stopping can take about twice as far as on a dry road.

quests.instruction: Which weather can delay flights and ferries because it is unsafe to travel in?
quests.hint: Look for thunder, lightning, and strong wind.
quests.explanation: Storms bring strong winds, big waves, and lightning. Airlines and ferry companies often wait until it is safe.
quests.funFact: Pilots plan routes to fly around big storm clouds.

quests.instruction: Which planet do rockets blast off from when they carry people and satellites to space?
quests.hint: Look at where you are standing right now.
quests.explanation: Rockets launch from Earth. They have to travel very fast to escape the pull of Earth's gravity.
quests.funFact: Rockets are launched from special places called spaceports.

quests.instruction: Which neighbour of Earth did astronauts fly to in a rocket in 1969?
quests.hint: It shines in our night sky.
quests.explanation: In 1969, the Apollo 11 mission carried astronauts to the Moon. They landed there in a small spacecraft.
quests.funFact: Apollo 11 took about three days to travel from Earth to the Moon.

quests.instruction: Who travels into space in a rocket or spacecraft?
quests.hint: This traveller wears a special suit and floats when far from Earth.
quests.explanation: An astronaut is trained to live and work in space. They travel in spacecraft and wear spacesuits for protection.
quests.funFact: Yuri Gagarin became the first person in space in 1961.

quests.instruction: In Venice, Italy, the old city has canals instead of streets. Which vehicle works like a bus on the water?
quests.hint: It floats, and it makes regular stops, just like a bus stop.
quests.explanation: Venice's water buses carry people along the canals and stop at landings. They work like buses, but on water.
quests.funFact: Venice's water buses are called vaporetti.

quests.instruction: In the Netherlands, many people ride this two-wheeler to school and work along special cycle paths. Which is it?
quests.hint: It has no engine, and the riders use their own legs.
quests.explanation: The Netherlands has flat land and lots of cycle paths, so cycling is an easy, everyday way to travel.
quests.funFact: The Netherlands has more bicycles than people.

quests.instruction: In Hong Kong, double-decker vehicles run on rails along the city streets. Which are they?
quests.hint: They run on rails in the street, not underground and not on tyres.
quests.explanation: Hong Kong's trams run on rails set in the street. Many have two floors, so they carry lots of passengers.
quests.funFact: Hong Kong's double-decker trams have been running since 1904.

quests.instruction: At an airport, where do officers check passports and bags when you arrive from another country?
quests.hint: This check happens after the flight, before leaving the airport.
quests.explanation: Customs and passport checks help countries keep track of who and what is coming in. Travellers wait in line to show their documents.
quests.funFact: Some airports have separate lines for travellers who have things to declare and those who do not.

quests.instruction: After your flight lands, where do you wait to collect your suitcase?
quests.hint: A moving belt carries the bags round and round.
quests.explanation: Baggage claim is where your checked bags arrive after a flight. You watch the belt and pick out your own.
quests.funFact: Many baggage belts form a loop, so bags keep going round until someone picks them up.

quests.instruction: What does a timetable show, so you know when to be at the bus stop or station?
quests.hint: Look at the numbers next to each stop or station.
quests.explanation: A timetable lists the times that buses, trains, or ferries leave. Checking it helps you arrive on time.
quests.funFact: Many stations show live times on big screens that update when services run late.

quests.instruction: In an old town with very narrow, crowded lanes, which vehicle can squeeze through most easily?
quests.hint: Choose the smallest one with an engine.
quests.explanation: Small, narrow vehicles fit through tight spaces. Large trucks and buses need wide roads.
quests.funFact: Some old towns have lanes so narrow that even a car cannot enter.

quests.instruction: A swimmer needs help quickly on a big lake. Which vehicle can reach them fastest?
quests.hint: Only one of these can go where the swimmer is.
quests.explanation: A fast boat can cross open water quickly. Lifeguards and rescue teams use boats to reach people in trouble.
quests.funFact: Many lifeguard services use small, fast boats to reach swimmers.

quests.instruction: A remote village has only a short grass airstrip. Which small aircraft could land there?
quests.hint: Big jets need long, hard runways. Think smaller.
quests.explanation: Small planes need much less space to take off and land than big airliners, so they can reach remote places.
quests.funFact: Australia's Royal Flying Doctor Service uses small planes to reach people in remote areas.

quests.instruction: A factory wants to send thousands of tonnes of goods across the ocean. Which is the most practical choice?
quests.hint: Think about which one can carry the biggest load over water.
quests.explanation: Ships can carry far more cargo than planes, and they cost less per box. A truck cannot cross the ocean.
quests.funFact: Most of the world's traded goods, by weight, travel by sea.

quests.instruction: A whole class of 40 children is going on a trip to a museum across town. Which vehicle carries them all together?
quests.hint: They need one vehicle with lots of seats.
quests.explanation: A bus can carry a whole class in one trip. Using cars would take many vehicles and many drivers.
quests.funFact: One bus can take the place of many cars on the road.

quests.instruction: A park path is closed to cars but open to people riding for fun and exercise. Which can use it?
quests.hint: Choose the vehicle that is small, quiet, and has no engine.
quests.explanation: Park paths are built for walkers and cyclists. They keep people away from fast traffic.
quests.funFact: Many cities are adding more cycle paths so people can ride away from cars.
